title: Replace confusing reasoning protocol flags with explicit model controls
description: The user found Model default and On confusing as effort options. Both resolve to High for the pinned IFM models. Show explicit per-model levels, use a truthful toggle for binary-only models, and preserve existing preferences and history.
acceptance_criteria: Given verified IFM capabilities, when viewing Settings or the composer, then effort choices are None, Low, Medium and High with no Model default or On options.
Given old IFM default/on preferences, when capabilities load, then both display as High through verified per-model aliases without an automatic preference write or a falsely dirty form.
Given named hosted capabilities, when choosing a GPT model, then its own supported choices including xhigh/max remain available.
Given verified binary-only reasoning, when editing it, then a Reasoning toggle uses the supported Boolean controls without invented effort levels.
Given unavailable or incomplete capabilities, when models refresh, then selections are preserved and unproven alias targets or settings remain unavailable.
Given historical messages, when viewing them after this update, then their original generation settings and provenance remain unchanged.
test_cases: Backend alias derivation from canonical metadata and exact verified mappings; hosted isolation and raw compatibility.
Settings/composer explicit choices, alias/default comparison, readiness transitions and binary controls.
Request payloads use explicit levels; browser checks preserve defaults and make no paid calls.
verification: TDD: initial backend 32 failed/4 passed, frontend 18 failed/33 passed; explicit-choice and terminal-alias defects reproduced before fixes. Final full backend 409 passed (43.86s), frontend 392 passed (61.84s), strict TypeScript/ESLint and build passed. Full 12 E2E passed (1.9m) before final producer correction; final E2E-12 passed (24.5s) after fixture API/model-worker restart. Independent frontend 53 tests and final backend 39 unit + 5 SQL passed. Actual ready 3.7B metadata returned direct default/on-to-high aliases. Desktop/mobile Light/Dark browser checks used legacy preference GET fixtures only, showed four choices with no false dirty state, issued zero mutations and preserved persisted defaults. Final source OpenAPI byte-matched generated TypeScript. Raw API flags, histories, provenance and UUID replay remain compatible. No weights, inference, merge or push.
